title: 对称三相电源的相电压与线电压
statement: 图示对称三相电源作星形（Y）连接，正序（A→B→C），N 为中性点。相电压有效值 220 V，以 U̇_A = 220∠0° V 为参考相量：U̇_B = 220∠−120° V，U̇_C = 220∠120° V。
求线电压 U̇_AB 的有效值和初相，以及 U̇_CA 的初相。

questions.explain: arctan(190.5/330) = 30°：线电压 U̇_AB 超前相电压 U̇_A 30°。

questions.ask: 对称 Y 形电源中，线电压与相电压的关系是：
choices: U̇_AB = √3·U̇_A∠30°（线电压是相电压的 √3 倍，超前对应相电压 30°）
U̇_AB = √3·U̇_A∠−30°（线电压滞后对应相电压 30°）
U̇_AB = U̇_A（Y 形连接时线电压等于相电压）
choiceExplain: 滞后 30° 是负序（A→C→B）电源的情况，或者和 Δ 负载“线电流滞后相电流 30°”记混了；正序时 −U̇_B 在 +60° 方向，U̇_A − U̇_B 落在 U̇_A 与 −U̇_B 的角平分线上。
线电压等于相电压的是 Δ 形连接；Y 形连接时线电压是两个相电压之差，模是相电压的 √3 倍。
2 倍是把两个相电压的模直接相加（当成同相）；线电压是相量之差，U̇_A 与 −U̇_B 相差 60°，合成的模只有 √3 倍。
questions.explain: 由相量图，U̇_A 与 −U̇_B 相差 60°、模相等，二者之和的模为 2 × 220 × cos30° = √3 × 220，方向在两者的角平分线上，即超前 U̇_A 30°。注意线电压是两相电压之差，不是之和。

hints: 线电压是两根端线之间的电压：U̇_AB = U̇_A − U̇_B（KVL）。
U̇_CA = U̇_C − U̇_A，也可以直接用规律“线电压 = √3 × 相电压，超前 30°”。
solution: **4. 规律。** U_l = √3·U_p，线电压超前对应相电压 30°；三个线电压同样对称，U̇_AB + U̇_BC + U̇_CA = 0（相电压之和也为 0）。我国低压配电“220/380 V”就是这个关系。

en.title: Phase and line voltages of a balanced three-phase source
statement: The balanced three-phase source is wye (Y) connected with positive sequence (A→B→C); N is the neutral point. The rms phase voltage is 220 V; take U̇_A = 220∠0° V as the reference: U̇_B = 220∠−120° V, U̇_C = 220∠120° V.
Find the rms value and phase of the line voltage U̇_AB, and the phase of U̇_CA.

questions.explain: U̇_AB = U̇_A − U̇_B = 220∠0° − 220∠−120° = 330 + j190.5 V, whose magnitude is √3 × 220 ≈ 381.05 V (the “380 V” of practice).
arctan(190.5/330) = 30°: the line voltage U̇_AB leads the phase voltage U̇_A by 30°.
U̇_CA = √3·U̇_C∠30° = 381.05∠(120° + 30°) = 381.05∠150° V. The three line voltages are balanced too, 120° apart.

questions.ask: In a balanced Y source, the line and phase voltages are related by:
choices: U̇_AB = √3·U̇_A∠30° (√3 times the phase voltage, leading the corresponding phase voltage by 30°)
U̇_AB = √3·U̇_A∠−30° (lagging the corresponding phase voltage by 30°)
U̇_AB = U̇_A (in a Y connection line and phase voltages are equal)
U̇_AB = 2·U̇_A (the two phase voltages simply add)
choiceExplain: Lagging by 30° is what a negative-sequence (A→C→B) source gives, or a mix-up with the Δ-load rule "line current lags phase current by 30°"; in positive sequence −U̇_B points at +60°, and U̇_A − U̇_B lies on the bisector of U̇_A and −U̇_B.
Line voltage equals phase voltage in a Δ connection; in a Y connection the line voltage is the difference of two phase voltages, √3 times as large.
A factor of 2 comes from adding the two magnitudes as if the phases were in step; the line voltage is a phasor difference, and U̇_A and −U̇_B are 60° apart, giving only √3.
questions.explain: From the phasor diagram, U̇_A and −U̇_B have equal magnitude and are 60° apart, so their sum has magnitude 2 × 220 × cos30° = √3 × 220 and lies on the bisector, 30° ahead of U̇_A. Note that a line voltage is the difference of two phase voltages, not their sum.

hints: A line voltage is the voltage between two lines: U̇_AB = U̇_A − U̇_B (KVL).
Write U̇_B = 220∠−120° in rectangular form, −110 − j190.5, and subtract.
U̇_CA = U̇_C − U̇_A, or use the rule “line voltage = √3 × phase voltage, leading by 30°”.
solution: **4. The rule.** U_l = √3·U_p, and each line voltage leads the corresponding phase voltage by 30°; the line voltages are balanced as well, U̇_AB + U̇_BC + U̇_CA = 0 (and so are the phase voltages). This is the familiar 220/380 V low-voltage supply.
